..
Today through Wednesday...

Shortwave ridging will move through the region today, bringing
calm and dry conditions. High temperatures are forecast to be in
the upper 30s and 40s. The chance for precipitation is very low 
across the lower elevations (less than 15%). There is a low chance
for showers over the southwest aspects of the Absaroka/Beartooths
this afternoon, though little impacts are expected.

Friday through the weekend, forecast certainty remains moderate.
The highest confidence with an approaching series of troughs is
that normal to slightly below normal temperatures are forecast
into next week, with highs in the 30s and 40s. The latest 
ensemble runs are consistent in showing an initial trough spilling
into the Rockies from the West Coast. This will bring Pacific 
moisture into the Northern Rockies, though the main trough energy 
and influence will be too far south for impacts to the forecast 
area. A secondary trough is shown dropping through Alberta Friday 
through Saturday. This trough will look to tap into the available 
moisture in place from the preceding trough. At the surface, a low
will develop over Central Wyoming through today. This will bring 
windy conditions to southeast Montana this afternoon and evening, 
with east to southeast winds gusting in the 25 to 40 mph range.

A cold front looks to nudge the surface low in Wyoming as well as
another low in Colorado eastward. These eventually coalesce over
the Northern Plains as the initial upper trough begins to 
influence the upper pattern. The cold front will shift winds to
the west-northwest across southern Montana and northern Wyoming
through early Friday morning. The latest GFS and ECMWF 
deterministics show showers over the far southwest mountains, with
precipitation spreading across the area by Friday evening. There 
is a potential window for upslope flow on N-NE aspects Friday 
evening as another cold front moves across the area. This window 
looks brief on cross-sections, with weak frontogenesis developing 
along the Beartooth/Red Lodge Foothills and moving eastward. Any 
upslope flow does not look to be very robust at this time, though
light snow accumulations are possible. On the other hand, Friday 
is beginning to come into Hi-Res model range and details remain
unclear. The latest run of the HRRR is showing precipitation
beginning as early as Friday morning and bringing several tenths
of precipitation across portions of south-central Montana. It then
continues spreading precipitation eastward by early Friday
afternoon. Note, this would be taking place in advance of the
main influence from the Canadian system. This appears to be an
outlier as the RRFS is depicting weak showers ahead of the parent
cold front coming out of central Montana late Friday morning.

The impacts from the trough dropping out of Canada and into 
Montana will increase on Saturday, with the chance for 
precipitation becoming moderate for much of the forecast area. 
Snowfall is likely in the mountains while a rain/snow mix will 
impact the plains. Light snow accumulations up to an inch are 
possible for the lower elevations. The latest probabilities from 
the NBM are low to moderate for portions of south-central Montana 
and northern Wyoming. The best chance for the lower elevations at 
this time exist west of Billings as well as along I-90 through 
Sheridan. The latest 48 hour probability for an inch of snowfall 
in Billings Friday evening through Sunday evening is 25%. For the
Sheridan Foothills, frontogenesis may develop allowing for better
precipitation efficiency. The current probability for at least 1
inch of snowfall in the Sheridan area is 50 to 70% while foothill
locations are as high as 90%. The majority of precipitation looks
to occur Friday night through Saturday afternoon, including any
snow accumulations. It is too soon to determine if products will
be needed though the most impacted locations are likely to be
amongst the mountains and foothills of southern Montana and
northern Wyoming.

The chance for precipitation will taper off into Sunday, with a
few lingering showers around. Accumulations and impacts will be
minimal with any activity on Sunday. The upper trough will quickly
move into the Upper Midwest through Sunday, leaving cooler
temperatures around. A weak shortwave is shown moving through late
Sunday, the only impacts being additional snow showers around and
west of Billings.

An additional trough may impact the Rockies early next week.
However, details remain unclear at this time. The latest track 
from ensembles would not be a favorable one for the Northern 
Rockies.

Continue to monitor the forecast as an active pattern approaches.
Matos
